units.text: 9 月 10 日，苹果正式发布 iPhone 18 Pro 系列，别看 iPhone 18 标准版还没影呢，“18”这个名号已经提前过气，喜提“牛夫人体验卡”。
那新晋“小甜甜”是谁？当然是下一代 iPhone，按正常逻辑，它该叫 iPhone 19 Pro，但种种迹象表明，苹果大概率要整活：直接叫 iPhone 20 Pro 系列。
为啥？因为苹果正好迎来 iPhone 问世 20 周年，这种大节点，不整点仪式感说不过去。
要知道，苹果是有“前科”的：上一个十年，就没发 iPhone 9，直接掏出 iPhone X；既然当年能跳过 9，如今再跳过 19，好像也很“苹果”。
虽说离传闻中的 iPhone 20 Pro 系列登场还有一年，但苹果新机的流量，懂的都懂，真机连影子都没有，“网络发布会”已经开了小半年。最开始，大家给它起的名字也很直白 ——“iPhone 20 周年纪念版机型”。
不过，名字叫啥都是虚的，有没有狠活儿才是硬道理。不止一个线人打包票：这机器会是真正的大改款，iPhone 要迎来一次大变革。
既然气氛都烘托到这儿了，各位IT之家家友对 iPhone 20 Pro 的好奇心估计早就压不住了吧？那还等啥，超前瞻小编这就安排！
一、iPhone，曲了 ~
提起 iPhone，最大的标签之一就是“直屏钉子户”，当年曲面屏火得一塌糊涂，安卓旗舰一个比一个弯，苹果愣是纹丝不动。
但要是跟你说，明年 iPhone 20 Pro 系列要投奔曲面屏，你信不？这事儿基本已经板上钉钉了。
最早在去年 5 月，彭博社、The Information 和 ETNews 先后跳出来放料，说苹果正琢磨着给 2027 年的 iPhone 20 周年纪念版来一次“底朝天”式重新设计。具体怎么个事呢？
彭博社：几乎全玻璃、曲面屏且无任何挖孔的 iPhone
The Information：至少有一款新 iPhone 将配备真正的无边框显示屏
ETNews：屏幕不仅会在左右两侧弯曲，还会延伸至顶部和底部边缘，带来真正的无边框视觉体验
按照这帮人的说法，这机器是 Pro 机型，屏幕完全看不到边框，直接环绕机身四个边。
不过在当时，这些传言实在太过“前瞻”，基本没人当真。毕竟把 iPhone 和曲面屏这俩词放一块儿，搁谁谁敢信啊？
然而，从今年开始，随着更多细节被扒出来，这事儿越来越不像空穴来风了。
今年 1 月，@phonefuturist 先行放料，晒出一份据称来自三位苹果工程师的 Telegram 聊天记录，有两句话得划重点：
并非采用类似三星 Note Edge 的真曲面显示屏，而是“四曲面玻璃覆盖在平面显示屏之上”；OLED 面板本身保持平面，所有的弧度完全体现在盖板玻璃上。
翻译成人话就是：苹果并非要在显示架构上进行革新，而是试图通过光学与工业设计手段，打造一种“伪曲面”效果，制造“隐形边框”的错觉。
到了 7 月，古尔曼坐不住了，加码爆料：这款 iPhone 会用曲面屏，机身背面重新用上玻璃面板，曲面玻璃直接包住边缘。
但苹果不打算复刻“瀑布屏”，而是搞等深四曲面，屏幕不会大幅度往侧边弯，用弧度浅浅的微曲面，滑动更顺手，握持也更舒服。
并且苹果还可能用上光学折射、导光结构这些花活，让你几乎看不到边框。
进入 8 月，Yogesh Brar 更狠，直接放出新渲染图，正面四曲面屏，背面也曲面，前后一起弯，iPhone 又圆润回去了。
图片还显示这机器用上了后置水平双摄，整体风格有点网传 iPhone Air 2 那味儿。
不光海外媒体们忙活，国内的消息源也没闲着，就拿爆料博主来说，关于 iPhone 20 Pro 系列的料，少说发过五次。
最有画面感的是 8 月 12 日那条： iPhone 20 Pro 系列手机内部代号 V73/V74，从供应链摸到的两块新屏物理尺寸增大，屏幕比例不变，有望引入全新无边四曲面设计。
该博主表示，苹果的无边四曲面猜测是 2D 直屏 + 玻璃盖板，利用玻璃的光学折射和形态设计，营造出视觉无边的效果，再结合液态玻璃 UI，可呈现软硬件相得益彰的效果。
总之，iPhone 20 Pro 系列到底会不会用曲面屏，在真机亮相之前，当然可以选择不信。
二、真全面屏，没了？
从刘海到药丸，苹果这些年致力于把屏幕顶上那点碍眼的开孔，一点点抠小。
今年的 iPhone 18 Pro，灵动到开孔面积直接缩了 35%，一举成为“史上屏占比最高的 iPhone”，可是大伙儿真正想要的，是一整块屏，一个孔都不留。
好消息是，iPhone Duo 的内屏已经把屏下摄像头安排上了，这不禁让不少果粉做个梦：到了 iPhone 20 Pro 系列，苹果会不会把“真全面屏 iPhone”从传闻里拽出来变成现实？
既然话都说到这份上了，iPhone 20 Pro 系列当真能把屏幕开孔干掉？按初期的风声，苹果确实有这个打算。
去年 5 月，《The Information》就报道说，苹果有望在 2027 年实现前设计主管乔纳森 · 伊夫多年来的梦想 —— 推出一款真正的全面屏 iPhone。
消息人士透露，至少一款 2027 年发布的新 iPhone 将配备真正的无边框显示屏，前置摄像头和 Face ID 系统全给塞到屏幕底下。
爆料博主那边也没闲着，直接放话：“看供应链信息，苹果接下来三年 ID 设计将大变。”
其中 2027 年那栏写得明明白白：全面大变 → 全面屏 (屏下 Face ID + 前摄)。
到了更晚的 12 月，韩媒 Dealsite 又再度确认：苹果将在 2027 年推出 iPhone 20，直接跳过 iPhone 19 这个命名，给初代 iPhone 诞生 20 周年献礼。
还特意强调，这台机器预计 2027 年第三季度发布，采用“真全面屏”设计，机身正面不再有任何可见开孔。
不过，不知道各位IT之家家友有没有留意，小编刚才用的是“初期”。为啥非要强调这俩字？因为后来的剧情，它拐弯了。
之前传的是，苹果想让这台 20 周年纪念版 iPhone 彻底干掉屏幕开孔，Face ID 和前摄全藏屏幕底下，正面干干净净，一个孔都不留，并且消息人士指出：苹果正在研发一种“拼接微透玻璃”，想让 Face ID 的红外传感器能穿透屏幕干活。
结果，显示行业分析机构 DSCC 的研究员 Ross Young 直接一盆冷水泼下来：这技术，2027 年很难成熟。
包括 Yogesh Brar 之前甩出来的渲染图里，正面也明晃晃留着一个前置单挖孔。
到了 9 月 21 日，爆料博主又出来补料，先剧透了 iPhone 20 Pro 系列早期屏幕的部分参数：
参数看着挺唬人，但重点在后头。该博主随后表示，苹果正测试无边四曲面设计，屏幕打孔方案是 —— 小灵动岛。
在评论区中，有网友提问“还是没法全面屏吗”，博主的回复很扎心：直板机短期内不会上......
所以说，绕了一大圈，梦里的屏下 Face ID + 前摄，终究只是一场梦，那个一个孔都没有的终极形态，还得继续等。
三、黑科技有戏也有变数
别觉得“曲屏”和“单打孔”只是小修小补，对苹果来说，这俩随便拎一个出来，都算得上“违背祖训”级别的大动作。
一个让直屏钉子户终于弯了，一个让灵动岛瘦成了单打孔，俩 buff 一叠，iPhone 20 Pro 系列基本可以提前锁定“大变革”三个字。
除此之外，iPhone 20 Pro 系列还流出了不少细节，同样值得蹲一波落地。
先看屏幕参数。跟 iPhone 18 Pro / Max 的 6.3 英寸和 6.9 英寸比，iPhone 20 Pro 系列直接涨到 6.41 英寸和 6.96 英寸。
据说 iPhone 18 Pro Max 的物理尺寸其实是 6.86 英寸，宣传写 6.9 英寸；到了 iPhone 20 Pro Max，物理尺寸 6.96 英寸，那大概率就要宣传成 7 英寸了。
接着唠影像。有小道消息说，苹果正在憋个大招 —— 自研 LOFIC 图像传感器，而且头一回就要塞进 iPhone 20 Pro 系列里。
这玩意儿要是真成了，iPhone 的成像能力会起飞：一次快门，亮部暗部全都要。高光不再过曝成一片白，暗部也不会糊成一团黑，细节全给你留住。
最后看芯片。今年 iPhone 18 Pro 系列搭载的 A20 Pro，已经率先吃上台积电 2nm 工艺；到了明年，iPhone 20 Pro 系列的 A21 Pro，制程还是 2nm，但会升级成 N2 效能增强版。
说白了，A20 Pro 是首批 2nm，A21 Pro 是 2nm 的“Pro 版”。
但是 ——IT之家小编必须说个但是了。早前有消息称，iPhone 20 Pro 系列准备上俩硬菜：CoE 和 LTPO+。
CoE 是 Color Filter on Encapsulation 的缩写，直译为封装彩色滤光片，指将显示屏所需的彩色滤光结构整合至封装层附近或面板内部，可减少部分传统光学结构占用的空间。
而 LTPO+ 是指低温多晶氧化物增强型屏幕，是以氧化物晶体管替代部分 LTPO 驱动晶体管的显示背板技术方案。显示背板负责驱动像素发光和刷新，可以减少准分子激光退火（ELA）等制造工序，并改善面板能效。
可是最新情报显示，苹果暂缓采用这俩技术。原因很现实：内存价格飙得太猛，制造成本已经够喝一壶了，再上 CoE 和 LTPO+ 这种烧钱货，物料成本要原地起飞。
除此之外，坊间还飘着不少关于 iPhone 20 Pro 系列的“可能升级”：固态按键、双层 OLED 屏、屏下发声、反向无线充电、超瓷晶 Ultra 高硬度玻璃……
但还是那句老话，饼画得再圆，也得看新 CEO 特努斯点不点头。毕竟传闻归传闻，最终能不能落地，还得看这位新掌门的想法。
四、总结
关于 iPhone 20 Pro 系列，IT之家小编今天就先扒到这儿。未来一年，爆料注定是一波接一波，随着时间推移，这台机器的真面目也会一点点浮出水面。
总之，iPhone 20 Pro 这盘菜，料是越下越猛，至于最后端上桌是满汉全席，还是熟悉的苹果式刀法，咱们明年见分晓。

units.text: Square sellers are now able to link accounts to Apple Business and manage information shown across Apple services from the Square Dashboard.

The integration, announced Thursday, means businesses using Square no longer need to update basic information, such as hours, address, and phone number, separately through Apple Business. Changes made through Square can instead be synced across Apple Maps, Wallet, Siri AI, and other Apple Apps.

Once connected, sellers can manage their logo and business information for Apple Maps place cards from the Square Dashboard. They can also add action links, such as viewing a menu, ordering food, scheduling an appointment, or booking.
In the United States and Canada, eligible Square sellers without an Apple Business account can also enroll via Square Dashboard.
Square says the integration is available to eligible businesses with physical locations in Australia, Canada, France, Ireland, Japan, Spain, the United Kingdom, and the United States.

In 2026, Apple merged all of its enterprise tools into a single platform dubbed Apple Business. It includes tools for device management, employee services, and managing how businesses appear across Apple services.

units.text: Apple TV is getting an early start on the holidays, today announcing two new holiday specials coming soon plus free offers for beloved Peanuts favorites. Here are the details.
New Peanuts and Fraggle Rock holiday specials, family movie with Chris Pratt, and more coming to Apple TV
Apple has two all-new holiday specials premiering this year from beloved properties:
“Snoopy Presents: 12 Days of Snoopy” will debut Friday, November 13
“Fraggle Rock: A Holiday Gift” will follow on Friday, December 4
Each new film adds to the existing catalog of Peanuts and Fraggle Rock offerings on Apple TV.

In its press release on holiday releases, Apple TV also spotlights the new family-friendly film Way of the Warrior Kid. It premieres Wednesday, November 25 and stars Chris Pratt and Linda Cardellini. Though it isn’t holiday-centric, Apple likes to debut new family films around Thanksgiving every year. Here’s the movie summary:

Middle school has been a nightmare for Marc (Jude Hill), a good kid who’s bullied by his classmates and feels like he’s behind in everything, from academics to P.E. to just making friends. That changes when his injured Uncle Jake (Pratt), a decorated Navy SEAL, comes to spend the summer and recuperate with Marc and his mom, Sarah (Cardellini). To help Marc defend himself, Jake devises an ambitious program he calls “Operation Warrior Kid” based on his SEAL training. Instead of teaching his nephew how to fight, Jake shows Marc what real courage is, facing down his own demons along the way.
Beyond this year’s new premieres, Apple is also offering free access to beloved Peanuts holiday specials on select weekends later this year. Here are the dates:
It’s the Great Pumpkin, Charlie Brown: October 17-18
A Charlie Brown Thanksgiving: November 14-15

units.text: I’ve been using Photoshop’s generative AI features to remove unwanted objects and extend photos since Adobe introduced them in 2023. They’ve been hit or miss for me, but they’re certainly a lot faster than the old-fashioned approach of masking, cloning, and manually painting things out. But with iOS 27, Apple has significantly improved its Clean Up tool and introduced the new Extend tool, and I was curious to see how Apple’s offerings compare with Adobe’s. So, with the help of a friend, I put both to the test using a variety of photos to see how they stack up.

For this article, my friend Jürg was kind enough to provide several photos from his travels throughout Switzerland and Europe. He takes much better photos than I ever could, and takes pictures of more exciting subjects than my corner of Ohio has to offer. You can see more of his photography on Instagram. I narrowed the selection down to six photos: three to test object removal and three to test image extension.

All photos were shot on an iPhone 17 Pro Max and edited on an iPhone 18 Pro Max running iOS 27.0. The Clean Up tool in iOS 27 has three options: Auto, Fast, and High Quality. I left the setting on Auto for all three tests.

Photoshop tests were done on a MacBook Pro running Adobe Photoshop 27.10.0 using the “Firefly Fill & Expand” model. I selected the objects using either the Object Selection Tool or Lasso Tool, then chose Generative Fill and left the prompt box blank.

For the Extend tool, I used whatever extension Photos selected by default. The Extend tool in Photos limits how far you can expand the edges of an image, while Photoshop doesn’t have the same restriction. To keep the comparison as consistent as possible, I used the result from Apple’s Photos as my reference, and had Photoshop create something in a similar size.
I made every effort to keep the HDR appearance as consistent as possible between the photos edited in Photos on iOS 27 and those edited in Photoshop, but there was some minor variation.
Making things disappear
Left: Original photo Right: iOS 27 Clean Up

First up is the removal of this red chair in front of the yellow door. This was the first photo I tested with the new Clean Up tool, and I have to say, it left quite a positive impression. The result looks very believable, and the only real mistake I noticed is that the rivet behind the chair’s left armrest was also removed instead of being correctly reconstructed. It’s not something I’m convinced most people would notice, though, and it would be an easy fix to clone back in with Photoshop. I was particularly impressed by how the shadow beneath the chair was replaced with a texture that matches the surrounding scene while also maintaining the existing lighting.
Left: Original photo Right: Adobe Photoshop Generative Fill

Photoshop doesn’t do as good a job as Apple’s Clean Up tool here. The chair’s shadow remains and looks more like an oil stain. The door’s rivets are misaligned, and one is obviously missing. The replacement texture also contains significantly more visual artifacts. Overall, it isn’t nearly as clean or realistic as what Clean Up produced.
Left: Original photo Right: iOS 27 Clean Up

I was really impressed with Clean Up’s results here. Not only did it remove the plate with bread, but it also added a nice reflection of the mug and jars. Notice it even got the handle of the spoon right in the reflection. A nice detail. Clean Up also completely removed the plate’s shadow from the napkin. I thought removing a red plate from a red table of the same color might prove more of a challenge for Clean Up, but nope! If I had one nitpick, it’s that Clean Up left the crumbs from the plate, though removing them would be very easy to do by running Clean Up again over that area.
Left: Original photo Right: Adobe Photoshop Generative Fill

Photoshop removed the plate with bread well enough, but again, it had issues with leaving behind an out-of-place shadow. The napkin looks dirty or wet here, but at least Photoshop didn’t leave behind as many pesky crumbs.
Left: Original photo Right: iOS 27 Clean Up

This photo proved to be a much bigger challenge for Clean Up. After attempting to remove the man on the right, Clean Up left behind a garbled mess with plenty of obvious artifacts. The leaves are too chunky. It struggled in a similar way on the left side of the image, where the woman with white hair was standing behind the white flowers. Clean Up also left behind a “ghost” of the dog’s head, though it arguably blends in with the stone wall and is much more noticeable in this side-by-side comparison.
Left: Original photo Right: Adobe Photoshop Generative Fill

Photoshop had no issues removing the woman on the left behind the white flowers or the man on the right behind the leaves, realistically filling in both areas in the process. The end result is a very convincing photo that looks like nobody was ever there. Photoshop also avoided leaving behind any phantom shadows this time.
Adding to the picture
Left: iOS 27 Extend Right: Adobe Photoshop Generative Fill

I thought this photograph of these old, winding steps would make for a good test because I didn’t think it would be immediately obvious to either AI what it was looking at, and I was curious to see how each would interpret the scene. Or even what it would do with it. It looks like iOS 27’s Extend tool interpreted the photo as something more like a ceiling fan, rounding off the ends of the stairs as though they were blades. Photoshop, on the other hand, simply extended the stairs outward and did a surprisingly good job of matching the wood grain.
Left: iOS 27 Extend Right: Adobe Photoshop Generative Fill

Extend does an excellent job living up to its name here. It extends the scene really well and creates a very convincing final image. Notice the windows are believably repeated and the bridge on the right side of the photo, while arguably too smooth, still manages to look fairly convincing.

Now look at Photoshop’s attempt. Actually, Photoshop, did you even make an attempt? This is a complete failure by just about every measure. Pure, obvious AI slop. The windows and roofline in the upper-left corner of the photo look terrible. The bridge on the right doesn’t have anything resembling the realistic arch Apple created, and for some reason, Photoshop decided the waterfall should randomly change direction rather than continue along the existing river line.
Left: iOS 27 Extend Right: Adobe Photoshop Generative Fill

Extend again manages to create a convincing image that, while not perfect, is significantly better than what Photoshop produced. Extend creates a believable table with some books or magazines, and the flowers in the vase look much more realistic than those generated by Photoshop. The decorative ornamentation above the left door also matches the real ones in the photo surprisingly well. There is some strangeness on the right side of the photo, where Extend has added a radiator, a random power cord, and a table for some reason.

Perhaps the biggest difference between Extend and Photoshop is at the ceiling. Extend has recreated more of the wood from the opposite wall, while Photoshop has tried to turn it into something more like a structural beam.

Photoshop, meanwhile, can’t seem to generate an image without the telltale signs of AI slop. Its table has too many legs and appears to simply “break off” before blending into the floor. The ornamentation above the door is less convincing, missing one of the “swirls” and doesn’t have the textured paint found on the real ornamentation in the photo.
I wouldn’t say either is perfect, but when it comes to realism, I think Apple’s solution edges out Adobe’s.
The good, the bad, and the AI slop

It’s worth mentioning that Photoshop requires a subscription to use, but none of the features I tested consume generative AI credits. Adobe does give users the option to choose other AI models that may require credits, but I didn’t use those models in my tests. Apple, too, has made it clear that “usage limits may apply” to some Apple Intelligence features and may charge for expanded access in the future.

It’s clear that Apple has made significant improvements to the Clean Up tool over previous versions of iOS. I’ve tried it before and always found it underwhelming, but now it’s genuinely good. The new Extend tool is impressive as well, and I found it significantly better than Adobe’s offering in my tests. Adobe gives you unlimited refinements and the ability to adjust results with prompts, but I question the value of those benefits if additional generations and prompts simply churn out more obvious AI slop. Apple may be more limiting in this regard, but its initial results are much better to begin with.
Of course, results will vary depending on the photograph, the complexity of the scene, and what you’re asking the tools to do. These were simply the results I got from the photos I tested.
How about you: Have you had a chance to try out Apple’s new Clean Up and Extend tools? If so, what do you think?

多位新机首批用户在社交平台与苹果官方支持社区反映，当试图在暗光环境、特殊角度，或通过第三方应用程序调用Face ID进行生物识别支付与账户登录时，屏幕会瞬间冻结，随后设备进入黑屏并显示苹果标志进行软重启（Soft Reboot）。部分受影响的用户表示，该故障不仅破坏了日常解锁体验，还频繁导致未保存的应用数据丢失与支付中断。
苹果在回应媒体问询时表示，工程团队已成功复现该故障，并确认该问题源于新系统中针对面容识别传感器深度图谱处理算法的内存分配错误，并非硬件级别的模组缺陷。苹果强调，用户的生物识别数据安全性未受任何影响，且正在加速测试一个专项补丁程序。
官方表示，修补该Face ID重启漏洞的iOS系统更新已进入最后测试阶段，预计将在未来数天内作为紧急维护补丁面向所有受影响的设备进行推送。在此期间，苹果建议频繁遇到该问题的用户可暂时关闭第三方应用的Face ID验证权限，或改用传统数字密码进行过渡。

units.text: Square has announced a new integration with Apple Business that should make Apple Maps better for both businesses and users. Here are the details.
Square integration lets businesses easily keep Apple Maps listings up to date with accurate info
Have you ever been frustrated to learn that an Apple Maps business listing has outdated info? Maybe the listed hours are inaccurate, or it has an error in the address, phone number, and so on.
Square’s new integration with Apple Business should help. From the announcement:

Square today announced a new integration with Apple that enables Square sellers to connect their locations to Apple Business from their Square Dashboard, so they can seamlessly manage and synchronize key business location information that appears on Apple Maps. Rather than managing multiple channels separately, sellers can now maintain their Apple presence alongside the rest of their business in Square. The integration makes it easier for sellers to ensure Apple users see up-to-date and accurate information across Apple Maps, Siri AI, Apple Wallet and other Apple apps.
Per Square, this integration provides several key benefits to business owners. It lets them:
Manage their brand and add a logo across connected locations, allowing them to enhance and extend their brand presence to Apple Maps place cards, directly from Square Dashboard.

Automatically sync key business details for each connected location, such as hours, address, and phone number, so this information stays up-to-date and accurate across Apple Maps, Siri AI, Apple Wallet, and other Apple apps and services without manual updates.

Turn discovery into engagement across connected locations with action links such as Menu, Order, Pickup, Delivery, Book, or Schedule Appointment, so customers can take action directly from an Apple Maps place card.
The partnership sounds like a clear win for businesses, since so many already rely on Square. But it should result in a better Apple Maps experience for users over time too.
Business owners can learn more about the Square and Apple Business integration at squareup.com/partnerships/applebusiness.

units.text: On Monday, we reported on an issue where iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max users were seeing their phone freeze and reboot following a failed Face ID attempt. To us, it appeared to be a software glitch rather than an inherent hardware fault.
Apple has now confirmed to 9to5Mac that a software update to address this problem is in the works, and should be available early next week.
Although the bug did not seemingly affect all users, it was reasonably widespread based on social media and 9to5Mac reader reports.

At the time, we reproduced the problem on an iPhone 18 Pro device by obscuring our face with our hand as we attempted a Face ID authentication to access the Passwords app. The phone simply stops responding to touch input, and hard reboots after a few seconds. You could then find a panic log in the iPhone Analytics section of the Settings app.

iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max feature a redesigned Face ID sensor system, where the Infrared camera has moved behind the under the screen near where the clock is rendered in the status bar, resulting in a 25% smaller visible Dynamic Island.

As we reported earlier in the week, some customers had already attempted to resolve the rebooting problem by swapping their phone with a new device at Apple, thinking it was a hardware fault. To reiterate, this is not necessary with a software fix now confirmed to be on the way.
On a somewhat related note, Apple also just released watchOS 27.0.1 to fix a random restart issue with Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4.

units.text: Apple is about to release a new iPad mini. This will mark the first update to the device in two years, and it’s expected to be a big one. Here’s everything we know so far about the new iPad mini coming as soon as next month.
OLED display
By far the biggest change to the new iPad mini will be to the display. According to multiple sources, the iPad mini 8 will feature an OLED display.

This will be a dramatic improvement to the iPad mini’s current LCD panel. For users, the move to OLED means deeper blacks, richer colors, and better contrast. The iPhone X was the first iPhone to use an OLED display in 2017, while the OLED iPad Pro debuted in 2024.

One lingering question, though, is whether the new iPad mini will use a ProMotion display for refresh rates of up to 120Hz. According to a sketchy rumor last week, the new iPad mini won’t offer ProMotion support and will instead be limited to 60Hz.
This hasn’t been corroborated by any other sources, though, so I’m holding out hope this leak is incorrect.
New chip

The current iPad mini, released in October 2024, is powered by Apple’s A17 Pro chip. The new iPad mini will likely feature the A19 Pro or A20 Pro chip. This will offer a solid boost in performance, and could enable support for the most advanced Siri AI features in iOS 27.
Better water resistance
According to Bloomberg, Apple has tested a “redesigned casing” for the iPad mini that is water-resistant like the iPhone.

Whether or not this water-resistant casing pans out remains to be seen. However, it would make the iPad mini far more durable. It’d be especially notable for people who use it as an e-reader, as one of the top features of dedicated e-readers like the Kindle is water resistance.
New speaker technology

The iPad mini 8 might also be Apple’s first device with a revamped vibration-based speaker system. This vibration-based speaker system would let Apple remove speaker holes, aiding its work to make the device water-resistant.
In contrast, the iPhone has speaker holes, but Apple uses gaskets and adhesives to make the device water-resistant.
New iPad mini release date
According to the latest reporting from Bloomberg, Apple is aiming to release the OLED iPad mini as early as this October. It’s allegedly the “biggest overhaul to the iPad mini in half a decade.”

There’s no word on how much the new iPad mini will cost. Apple increased the price of the current iPad mini in July from $499 to $599 (currently discounted to $569 on Amazon). Whether the new iPad mini with OLED is even more expensive remains to be seen.
What do you think of Apple’s rumored plans for the iPad mini? Are you tempted by the OLED display? Let us know down in the comments.

Apple TV is expanding its holiday lineup with new specials starring Snoopy and the Fraggles. Both join a collection of returning seasonal favorites available to stream throughout the holidays.
"Snoopy Presents: 12 Days of Snoopy"
With the year winding down, the Peanuts gang is on their best behavior. Unfortunately, everyone's beloved beagle, Snoopy, has landed himself on the naughty list.

Snoopy's got 12 days to prove that he's not a bad dog, and along the way he'll discover that the holidays are about more than just presents. "Snoopy Presents: 12 Days of Snoopy" will premiere on Friday, November 13.
If you want more time with the Peanuts kids, you're in luck. Apple TV has a few more holiday specials to check out.

"The Snoopy Show - Happiness is Holiday Traditions" sees Snoopy and Woodstock visit Snoopy's brother, Spike, for Christmas. Spike makes his return in ""I Want a Dog for Christmas, Charlie Brown" when he visits the gang to cheer up Rerun.

And, of course, Apple TV is the only place you can stream "A Charlie Brown Christmas." Apple TV subscribers can watch at any time, but Apple is offering a limited-time free streaming window from Saturday, December 12 to Sunday, December 13 for anyone.
"Fraggle Rock: A Holiday Gift"
This all-new musical special from The Jim Henson Company premieres December 4 with a guest appearance by Nicole Scherzinger.

Wembley's new role as Spirit Captain sends him on a mission to bring holiday cheer to every corner of the Rock. But when the Fraggles swipe a treasured snow globe from Doc's workshop, Wembley has to set things right and discovers that the best way to spread joy is by helping others.
"Fraggle Rock: A Holiday Gift" premieres on Dec 4 | Image credit: Apple TV

If you're still itching for even more Fraggle Festivities, you can check out "The First Snow of Fraggle Rock." The Fraggles' holiday celebrations hit a snag when just one snowflake falls, and Gobo can't find the inspiration for a festive new song, sending him to Outer Space in search of some seasonal magic.

If you haven't tried it out yet, Apple TV offers a free, three-month trial when a first-time watcher buys a qualifying device, such as an iPhone. There is also a free seven-day trial, after which the monthly cost is $14.99 or $119.99 per year.

units.text: Unsurprisingly, Apple is working on an iOS 27 update that will fix an issue affecting some iPhone 18 Pro users where Face ID is failing and forcing a restart.

Whenever millions of devices are released alongside a new OS, there are problems. In the case of the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, some users reported restarts caused by kernel panics, so unexpected and unforced restarts.
One Reddit user said this happened when the Wallet app was opened. That same user, and two others, also reported crashes after Face ID failed to recognize them.
Now, Apple has confirmed that it is working on a software update that will fix this particular problem. No specific release date has been given but reportedly it will be early next week.
This does mean that Apple regards the bug as a software problem. However, the same Reddit user says that the company also considers their iPhone to be faulty and is replacing it.

Separately, AppleInsider has been told of users being unable to place calls on AT&T, which we are investigating now and will have information later on Thursday. Plus there were documented issues with sudden restarts on the Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4, but that has been patched.

evidence.discovery_lead: 快科技9月24日消息，自iPhone 18系列正式开售以来，市场热议声不断，“iPhone18第一批受害者”相关话题更曾冲上热搜榜单。 不少首发入手的网友吐槽新机升级幅度太小、实用性不及预期，没想到知名头部带货主播李佳琦，也成为了首批实测后直言“升级感知微弱”的用户之一。 近日，李佳琦在直播中公开分享了iPhone 18 Pro Max的使用体验，他坦言除了电量其他功能和iPhone17并无区别。 针对新机搭载的可变光圈影像升级，李佳琪直言：“ 就这个手机我体验下来只有电量的区别，没有任何的区别。 （定光圈）平时也不怎么用我也不拍照。一般人不会这样，我没那么专业。如果你们不那么追求最新款手机的话iPhone 17 Pro Max真够用了。 “我觉得红色比较好看，但是红色有个超级无敌大bug，巨粘指纹。 你们有时间红色去线下看一看摸一摸，为什么它的镜头盖上巨粘指纹，就是你一摸一层油。超粘指纹，粘疯了，所以我立马套了一个壳。 ”李佳琪评价称。 据了解，iPhone 18 Pro系列于9月18日正式全球开售，国行版本起售价9999元起，作为苹果年度顶级旗舰机型，新机发布前后始终占据数码圈热度榜首。 其中，新推出的勃艮第酒红色作为专属主打配色，凭借高级复古的质感、超高的辨识度，一经上市便火速登顶热搜，成为消费者首选的热门配色。 实际上，苹果历年新机的全新配色，向来是带动销量、制造话题的核心亮点。 去年iPhone 17系列推出的星宇橙色，就因配色质感与奢侈品牌爱马仕经典色系高度相似，被网友冠以“爱马仕橙”的称号，一度成为年度爆款手机配色。 而今年iPhone 18 Pro系列的勃艮第酒红色，同样延续了新配色的流量优势，凭借独特色调能让人一眼分辨出是新款机型，精准拿捏了用户追求差异化、辨识度的购机心理。

近日，李佳琦在直播中公开分享了iPhone 18 Pro Max的使用体验，他坦言除了电量其他功能和iPhone17并无区别。
针对新机搭载的可变光圈影像升级，李佳琪直言：“就这个手机我体验下来只有电量的区别，没有任何的区别。（定光圈）平时也不怎么用我也不拍照。一般人不会这样，我没那么专业。如果你们不那么追求最新款手机的话iPhone 17 Pro Max真够用了。
“我觉得红色比较好看，但是红色有个超级无敌大bug，巨粘指纹。你们有时间红色去线下看一看摸一摸，为什么它的镜头盖上巨粘指纹，就是你一摸一层油。超粘指纹，粘疯了，所以我立马套了一个壳。”李佳琪评价称。
据了解，iPhone 18 Pro系列于9月18日正式全球开售，国行版本起售价9999元起，作为苹果年度顶级旗舰机型，新机发布前后始终占据数码圈热度榜首。
其中，新推出的勃艮第酒红色作为专属主打配色，凭借高级复古的质感、超高的辨识度，一经上市便火速登顶热搜，成为消费者首选的热门配色。
实际上，苹果历年新机的全新配色，向来是带动销量、制造话题的核心亮点。
去年iPhone 17系列推出的星宇橙色，就因配色质感与奢侈品牌爱马仕经典色系高度相似，被网友冠以“爱马仕橙”的称号，一度成为年度爆款手机配色。
而今年iPhone 18 Pro系列的勃艮第酒红色，同样延续了新配色的流量优势，凭借独特色调能让人一眼分辨出是新款机型，精准拿捏了用户追求差异化、辨识度的购机心理。

units.text: I’ve been using iPhone 18 Pro for the past week after a full year as an iPhone Air user. And while there are advantages with each model, my main takeaway about iPhone 18 Pro so far is that it has zero compromises. Here’s what I mean.
iPhone 18 Pro: The best camera system, battery life, and performance
If you want to buy a new iPhone, chances are the iPhone 18 Pro is a strong contender.
I’ve had mine for a week now, a Burgundy model that replaced my iPhone Air. And despite loving the Air a lot, it’s hard to match Apple’s no-compromise approach to the iPhone 18 Pro.
Cameras are better and far more versatile on iPhone 18 Pro compared to the Air. Telephoto and Ultra Wide lenses are great for specific use cases, but even the Main camera is better on iPhone 18 Pro.

Battery life is similarly impressive. I generally found the iPhone Air’s battery good enough for everyday use, and only needed to charge mid-day occasionally. But with iPhone 18 Pro I don’t even have to think about battery.

Performance is fantastic too. The A20 Pro chip makes everything on the iPhone feel fast, and I’ve even noticed a more responsive Siri AI. Thanks to the vapor chamber, I haven’t had any issues of overheating either, which the Air sometimes struggled with.

I’m not a pro photographer, and if you want battery tests or performance benchmarks, my colleague Chance’s iPhone 18 Pro review has you covered. But after a week with iPhone 18 Pro, that word “best” keeps coming back to me.

iPhone 18 Pro (and Pro Max) pack the absolute best camera system Apple makes, have the best battery life, and perform better than any other models. I’ve even noticed smaller improvements: the better built-in speakers and Dynamic Island upgrades are highlights.

There are measurable differences in all these areas, but I also appreciate just knowing my iPhone has the “best” Apple offers in key areas that matter most. There’s no wondering: would these pictures of my family look better if I used a different iPhone? Would this slowdown have happened?
All the positives of iPhone 18 Pro aside though, I’ll admit that I’m still very intrigued by the forthcoming iPhone Duo.
iPhone Duo, like iPhone Air, will be compromised but so compelling
The iPhone Air and iPhone Duo share a lot in common. Besides having similar design traits, they also both have shortcomings.

Like my iPhone Air, the iPhone Duo will have a worse camera system than iPhone 18 Pro. Battery might be comparable but definitely worse than the Pro Max, and I suspect sustained performance will lag a bit too. iPhone Duo will also lack Face ID and the Action button.
Yet despite these compromises, I’m very excited to get my hands on the device.
That’s because it offers a lot of compelling innovations not found in iPhone 18 Pro. The foldable form factor represents arguably the biggest iPhone hardware change ever.
I’ve been enjoying my iPhone 18 Pro a lot. But guess what happened when I picked up the iPhone Air the other day?
I instantly said, “Wow.”
Here’s my iPhone 18 Pro Max review: Do not buy an iPhone Air unless you want to immediately return every other phone forever.
— Ben Thompson (@benthompson) September 21, 2026

The Air’s thinness had become the norm for me after a year of use. But several days into using iPhone 18 Pro, I was able to find fresh appreciation for how futuristic the Air feels. And I suspect iPhone Duo will evoke similar feelings—not just for its design, but its utility too.
I’m excited to have an iPad-like experience with the iPhone that fits in my pocket. That’s true despite being admittedly torn about the downsides the Duo will bring.

The days of Apple offering a single “best” iPhone are gone. If you want a model with zero compromises, iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max seem fantastic. But for something more futuristic and unique, I still can’t wait to try iPhone Duo.
Where do you stand on iPhone 18 Pro vs. iPhone Duo? Let us know in the comments.

据IT之家了解，苹果于 2010 年 7 月 16 日召开了这场新闻发布会。当时，部分用户反映，以特定方式握持 iPhone 4 可能导致手机蜂窝网络信号减弱，因此苹果决定对此作出回应。
在发布会的预先准备演讲中，乔布斯宣布，符合条件的 iPhone 4 用户可以免费获得保护套，同时苹果还提供 30 天退货选项。苹果后来公开了这部分演讲的视频，但没有发布问答环节。当时媒体主要通过文字报道和现场照片记录了这部分内容。
如今曝光的视频显示了此前未公开的问答环节。其中一个值得关注的片段发生在大约 18 分 45 秒处。格鲁伯当时提问，现场的 3 名苹果高管是否在自己的 iPhone 4 上使用保护套。
乔布斯、库克和曼斯菲尔德随后分别举起了自己手中的 iPhone 4，展示这些手机均没有安装保护套。
在之后的回答中，乔布斯还详细谈到了苹果从这场争议中获得的经验，包括为什么苹果当时选择先收集更多数据，然后才召开新闻发布会回应问题。
在视频接近尾声时，乔布斯还解释了苹果长期坚持掌握或控制产品核心技术的战略，以及随着软件在消费电子产品中的重要性不断提升，这种做法为什么变得越来越有价值。
并不清楚这段视频究竟来自何处，也不知道为什么直到现在才突然出现在网上。

units.text: Apple is testing iOS 27.0.1 for iPhone, according to web traffic analytics for 9to5Mac. The update will likely focus on bug fixes and performance improvements.
iOS 27.0.1 coming soon
iOS 27.0.1 started surfacing in 9to5Mac analytics a few days ago. MacRumors has reported the same.
Apple told 9to5Mac this morning that it will release a software update early next week to fix a problem causing some iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max units to restart after a failed Face ID attempt.
We covered the issue earlier this week, explaining that the issue occurs when you try to use Face ID to unlock an app like Passwords. If Face ID fails, your iPhone might unexpectedly reboot.

I was never able to reproduce this problem on my iPhone 18 Pro or iPhone 18 Pro Max, but it clearly affected a number of users. The good news is that it’s a bug that can be fixed via software, rather than any sort of hardware fault.
It’s likely, but not confirmed, that iOS 27.0.1 will address that problem. It could also include fixes for other bugs affecting iOS 27 and the new iPhone 18 Pro hardware.
Have you had any problems since updating to iOS 27? What about iPhone 18 Pro-specific problems? Let us know down in the comments.

往年.2 的测试版 10 月底才开始，今年 9 月中旬就来了，还直接跳过了 27.1 的测试版。因为 iPhone Duo 10 月 23 日发售，苹果官宣它出厂就装 27.1；外媒分析，要是提前放出 27.1 测试版，代码里藏的新机细节可能就漏了，所以干脆让开发者跳级测 27.2。
尽管 iOS 27.2 测试版早了一个多月，但正式版大概率要等在 10 月 23 日的 iPhone Duo 发售之后，这么一算感觉今年双十一还是有点难顶。

units.text: 高通9月24日宣布，已经与苹果延长芯片相关的专利许可协议，新协议将于2027年4月1日起生效。此次续约延续了两家公司在2019年结束长期专利与基带芯片纠纷后建立的合作关系，也意味着即使苹果持续扩大自研调制解调器芯片的使用范围，高通与苹果之间的专利授权关系仍将继续。
高通并未公布此次协议具体的商业条款，包括授权费用以及新协议的具体期限，两家公司也没有对外披露更多细节。
高通与苹果目前的合作关系源自2019年达成的一项全球性和解协议。在此之前，两家公司围绕无线通信专利授权费以及调制解调器芯片供应问题展开了长达两年的全球法律纠纷。
2019年4月，两家公司在美国加利福尼亚州圣迭戈的一场陪审团审判即将开始之际达成和解。根据当时的安排，苹果向高通支付了一笔未公开金额的款项，两家公司撤回全球范围内正在进行的诉讼，同时签署了一份为期六年的全球专利许可协议，协议自2019年4月1日起生效。
原协议同时赋予苹果将授权期限延长两年的选择权。随着此次续约，苹果实际上行使了这一延长安排，使双方原本持续至2027年3月底的专利许可关系继续向后延伸。
这份协议的重要性在于，它与高通向苹果供应通信芯片是两个相互关联但又有所区别的业务关系。即使苹果逐步减少对高通调制解调器芯片的依赖，高通仍然可以通过专利许可业务继续向苹果收取相关费用。
近年来，苹果一直在推进自研调制解调器芯片，并已经开始在部分产品中采用自研方案。随着苹果进一步扩大自研基带芯片的使用范围，高通来自苹果的芯片销售收入预计将持续下降。
高通首席执行官克里斯蒂亚诺·阿蒙此前已经表示，由于苹果增加使用自研调制解调器芯片，高通来自苹果产品的收入下降速度可能快于此前预期。高通此前预计下一代iPhone中采用高通组件的比例约为20%，但受到供应情况以及苹果自研芯片推进等因素影响，实际占比可能明显低于这一水平。
这意味着，高通与苹果之间的合作正在发生结构性变化：双方过去高度依赖的调制解调器芯片供应关系正在逐渐减弱，但围绕高通无线通信专利的授权关系仍然保持。
高通的专利授权业务由Qualcomm Technology Licensing负责运营，该部门管理高通的大量无线通信技术专利。即使设备制造商使用自己的调制解调器或从其他供应商购买芯片，只要相关产品使用了高通拥有的必要通信专利，仍可能需要按照双方达成的授权安排支付专利许可费用。
苹果近年来也在逐步降低对高通芯片的依赖。苹果此前已经推出自研调制解调器，并开始将其应用于部分iPhone产品。随着自研芯片技术进一步成熟，苹果未来可能在更多产品中减少高通芯片的使用。
不过，自研调制解调器并不意味着苹果与高通之间的专利关系会自动结束。通信标准涉及大量基础专利，即使一家厂商不使用某个特定供应商的芯片，也可能仍然需要获得相关标准必要专利的授权。因此，此次双方延长许可协议，与苹果是否继续采购高通调制解调器芯片并不是完全相同的问题。
2019年的和解也结束了当时两家公司在全球多个司法辖区展开的法律争端。当时苹果指控高通滥用其市场地位并收取过高的专利许可费用，而高通则反诉苹果违反相关协议并涉及专利问题。最终双方选择通过和解结束这场持续两年的全球诉讼。
此次协议延长表明，虽然苹果正在逐步摆脱对高通通信芯片的依赖，但双方目前仍然需要维持稳定的专利授权关系。对于高通而言，这也意味着在苹果芯片采购规模下降之后，其庞大的专利组合仍可以继续从苹果业务中获得授权收入。
对于苹果而言，延长协议则能够继续确保其产品在全球市场销售过程中获得必要的无线通信专利授权，同时避免双方再次围绕专利授权问题爆发类似2017年至2019年期间的大规模法律争端。
目前两家公司没有公布此次协议究竟延长多长时间，也没有披露新的授权费用安排。可以确定的是，新协议将从2027年4月1日开始生效。随着苹果继续推进自研调制解调器芯片，高通与苹果之间的关系未来将越来越从“芯片供应商与客户”转向“通信专利授权方与设备制造商”的关系。

The Wanted Man is new crime drama coming soon to Apple TV
Crime thrillers are one of Apple TV’s most popular genres, and the streamer just announced its latest offering that’s coming soon.
The Wanted Man premieres Wednesday, January 6 with its first two episodes, followed by weekly releases through February 17.

Hugh Laurie stars as a crime boss who’s betrayed by someone at his firm, is sent to prison, and plans to break out. The cast also includes Thandiwe Newton, Fionn Whitehead, Gina McKee, Hazel Doupe, Elliott Heffernan, and Stephen Dillane.
The Wanted Man hails from George Kay, the creator of Idris Elba thriller Hijack.
Here’s Apple’s official plot summary:

When organized crime boss Felix Carmichael (Hugh Laurie) is betrayed by someone inside his own firm and sent to the notorious Staplehurst prison, he’s forced to remember his own brutality to fight for survival. With his family, firm and fortune at stake, Felix resolves to do the unthinkable: escape.
If you’re looking for more crime-centric series, Last Seen and a new season of Slow Horses are both airing now, and will be joined next month by the Liev Schreiber-starring Nocturne.
Are you interested in watching The Wanted Man? Let us know in the comments.
Apple TV is available for $14.99 per month, or you can get it discounted through the Apple One bundle.

units.text: Providing no new details, Qualcomm has issued a statement confirming that it and Apple have renewed the existing patent licensing agreement first signed in 2019, with an effective date of April 1, 2027.
In one introductory sentence, and one quote, Qualcomm dropped the news of the renewal on the world. The first sentence states the agreement's effective date.
"We are pleased to extend the Apple license agreement," said John Han, Executive Vice President and General Manager of Qualcomm Technology Licensing in the second sentence.
That's it.

There are no details yet about how long the license pact is for. The last one had a five-year initial term, with a two-year extension possible. That two-year extension expires on the last day of March, 2027.
How we got here

In January 2017, Apple filed a lawsuit against Qualcomm, alleging the chip producer had withheld approximately $1 billion in royalty payments to Apple, in retaliation for cooperating with South Korean antitrust investigations, along with claims of extortion, monopolistic practices, and price gouging.
In the suit, Apple claimed Qualcomm insisted on charging Apple "at least five times more in payments than all the other cellular patent licensors we have agreements with combined."

Apple's lawsuit followed shortly after the U.S. Federal Trade Commission stepped in with its own suit, accusing Qualcomm of forcing Apple into a baseband exclusivity deal from 2011 until 2016, by offering lower royalty payments in the form of rebates.

The following April, Qualcomm made its own filing with the court denying Apple's complaint, accusing it of attempting to pay less than the fair market value for access to Qualcomm's standard essential payments, breach of contract, and wrongly inducing regulatory action in a number of jurisdictions, among other issues.

Once the exclusivity period ended, Apple started to diversify its modem suppliers to include Intel, but this partnership was also a source of issue for Qualcomm. In a filing from September 2018, Qualcomm claims Apple stole trade secrets relating to its intellectual property that it provided to Intel, specifically software used to improve the performance of its baseband chips.

It's not clear how much Apple is paying per iPhone equipped with a Qualcomm modem up to and including the iPhone 18 Pro Max US model. It is estimated that Apple is paying between $8 and $9 per device.
Apple's C2 modem is in Apple's US iPhone 18 Pro model.

units.text: 快科技9月24日消息，M6 Mac mini已经正式开售，标准版配备16GB统一内存和256GB SSD，但日本媒体AAPL Ch.拆机实测发现，256GB版的SSD读写速度只有512GB版的一半左右，苹果发布会宣称的“储存速度最高快2倍”只有512GB以上机型才能达到。
AAPL Ch.用Blackmagic Disk Speed Test对256GB版跑分显示，连续写入3000.2MB/s，连续读取3216.8MB/s。
对比Tom's Hardware用512GB版测到的数据为写入6577.4MB/s、读取6371.5MB/s，512GB版写入快了119%，读取快了98%，差不多整整一倍。
其他几家外媒用512GB版测出的成绩也都在6000MB/s以上。
主要原因在NAND芯片数量，SSD控制器可以同时对多颗NAND芯片读写，512GB版用两颗芯片，相当于双车道同时跑；256GB版只有一颗256GB芯片，只剩单车道。
当然这不是苹果第一次这么干，2022年M2 MacBook Air和2023年M2 Mac mini的256GB版同样是单颗NAND，当时也被测出比512GB版慢很多，M3 MacBook Air又改回了两颗的方案，M6 Mac mini再次回到了M2的做法。
苹果官方没有解释原因，比较可能的是成本考量，毕竟单颗256GB芯片比两颗128GB芯片便宜。
苹果在发布M6 Mac mini时宣称比M4快4倍AI性能、2倍储存和图形性能、40% CPU性能提升，但没有说明储存速度的提升跟容量有关。
同时苹果提供给大型科技媒体和知名博主的评测机都是512GB版，所以各家测出来的SSD速度确实都达到了官方宣称。
256GB版虽然比512GB慢很多，但并没有比上一代慢，和M4 256GB版相比，写入从2014.5MB/s提升到3000.2MB/s，快了49%，读取从2792.5MB/s提升到3216.8MB/s，快了15%。
和同样单颗NAND的M2 256GB版比，写入快86%，读取快了一倍多，因此M6 256GB版的SSD在历代标准版里其实是最快的，只是没达到苹果宣称的2倍。
除了速度和容量本身，购买256GB版本之前还有几个值得考虑的点，256GB扣掉macOS系统和内置应用后实际可用空间不多，装几套大型软件可能就满了。
更关键的是，M6 Mac mini的SSD直接焊在主板上，买了就不能升级，上一代M4 Mac mini的SSD还是模块化设计，也有第三方厂商推出了升级模块，但M6改回了焊接方案，事后升级这条路堵死了。
